messages:
tasha: FYI hit a nasty loop when using redwoodctl in WSL2 with a symlinked ~/.redwood to Windows. CLI writes token, then next run immediately POST 401 and does refresh attempts non-stop.

miguel: ugh. Did you install via the MSI or scoop? and which redwoodctl version?

tasha: MSI latest. redwoodctl 1.8.2. repro steps: on Windows host create ~/.redwood and symlink it into WSL via ln -s /mnt/c/Users/tasha/.redwood /home/tasha/.redwood. Then inside WSL: export REDWOODCTL_LOCALTEST=1; redwoodctl whoami -> starts auth then loop.

jyoti: That pattern rings a permissions and mtime issue. Windows NTFS sometimes reports mtime that confuses token TTL checks; CLI might treat refresh_token as still valid but server rejects it. Any logs?

tasha: pasted minimal scrubbed logs:
```
INFO  auth: starting device flow
DEBUG tokenstore: writing /home/tasha/.redwood/tokens/default.json
INFO  api: POST /token -> 200
INFO  auth: token issued, expires_in: 300
INFO  token: saved
INFO  api: POST /token -> 401 invalid_grant
ERROR auth: refresh failed
INFO  auth: retrying in 2s
```

paul: Two layers: (1) symlink + Windows antivirus sometimes keeps file handle open and writes flush late -> corrupt JSON read, (2) file ownership/UID mismatch causes tokenstore to read stale copy from host overlay. We saw similar in #1971234567 but not exactly the same.

miguel: Can you dump the token file after login and on next run compare bytes? also check fsnotify behavior — some apps rely on atomic rename and NTFS semantics differ.

tasha: Ran diff: host token.json contains both access_token and refresh_token. WSL copy shows same contents but with CRLF endings and an extra BOM char in front of file. That could break the parser.

jyoti: BOM/CRLF will definitely cause JSON parse issues sometimes; our tokenloader might silently ignore parse errors and fall back to stored values which then mismatch server expectations. Good catch.

paul: Short term workaround: normalize the token file after host writes: dos2unix + strip BOM. Or mount with metadata option?

tasha: I wrote a tiny entrypoint script that runs before redwoodctl: `sed -i '1s/^\xEF\xBB\xBF//' ~/.redwood/tokens/*.json && dos2unix ~/.redwood/tokens/*.json || true` — fixed my loop.

miguel: Nice. For the product fix we should: (A) be tolerant of BOM and CRLF when reading tokens, (B) offer a CLI-level opt to ignore any overlay-provided refresh tokens in localtest mode. Suggest `REDWOODCTL_IGNORE_OVERLAY_REFRESH=1` and `redwoodctl login --ephemeral` to force device flow.

jyoti: agreed. Also add a warning log if token JSON parse required normalization, so users see the source of the problem. Possibly a one-line telemetry event (not PII) for parse-fix action.

paul: I'll file a DX issue and draft an API/CLI spec: preserve existing behavior for hosted runs; when REDWOODCTL_LOCALTEST=1 or --ephemeral, CLI should delete refresh_token fields from loaded overlays and prefer device flow. Add unit tests for BOM/CRLF handling and for symlinked tokenstores with uid/gid mismatch.

devex-bot: created issue #2487: "redwoodctl: tolerate BOM/CRLF in token files; ignore overlay refresh_token in localtest / add --ephemeral flag" (assigned: eng-cli).

tasha: thanks all. I'll push the entrypoint script to our quickstart repo as a short-term note and attach logs to #2487. :raised_hands:
